title: Ferrous iron Promotes Fdred Synthesis in a Composite Microbial Consortium to Drive the Shift from Denitrification to DNRA
description: Conventional biological nitrogen removal processes are constrained by lengthy process chains and dependence on carbon sources, necessitating the development of novel enhanced nitrogen removal strategies with functional integration and operational stability. In this study, a synthetic bacterial consortium was constructed, consisting of the aerobic denitrifier Pseudomonas stutzeri, the facultative anaerobic denitrifier Klebsiella sp., and the heterotrophic nitrifying aerobic denitrifier Alcaligenes sp. The effects of five iron species - zero valent iron, ferrous iron, ferric iron, ferric oxide, and ferroferric oxide - as well as their combined effects with polyacrylamide, on nitrogen removal efficiency and oxidative stress responses of the consortium were investigated. Metagenomic sequencing was employed to elucidate the regulatory mechanisms of ferrous iron on metabolic processes. The results showed that ferrous iron enhanced nitrate removal efficiency and reduced intracellular oxidative stress by inducing the Fenton reaction extracellularly. Metagenomic analysis revealed that ferrous iron reshaped the carbon and nitrogen metabolic networks: in the carbon metabolic network, the enrichment of the por gene in the glycolytic pathway generated a large amount of reducing power in the form of reduced ferredoxin, which in turn promoted the enrichment of the dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium pathway, whereas denitrification was inhibited due to competition for electrons. Furthermore, iron metabolism provided sufficient prosthetic groups for iron dependent enzymes involved in carbon and nitrogen metabolism. This study elucidated the intrinsic mechanism by which ferrous iron promoted synergistic carbon and nitrogen removal, providing a theoretical foundation for the development of a multi-process coupled deep nitrogen removal system integrating "bioaugmentation, chemical regulation, and physical sedimentation".
